mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through lower cost of capital for corporate investments.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS predicting 20-day returns is below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window or average 20-day returns in low-rate periods (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it signals restrictive monetary policy that increases cost of capital and reduces corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC for FEDFUNDS predicting 20-day returns is below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts corporate earnings growth and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC for PAYEMS-UNRATE interaction term is below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, strong housing starts (HOUST > 1100 thousand units) and high real consumption (RSAFS > 450,000 million dollars) signal overvaluation and potential market correction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST > 1100 and RSAFS > 450,000 in late-cycle expansion (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC for HOUST-RSAFS interaction is below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity and economic expansion that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through stronger economic fundamentals.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO is above its 12-month moving average (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC for INDPRO predicting 60-day returns is below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1000 thousand units, it indicates contraction in the housing sector and weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through reduced economic activity.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST < 1000 (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC for HOUST predicting 5-day returns is below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high inflation rate (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) combined with a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) signals persistent inflation without adequate monetary tightening, increasing stagflation risk and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS < 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC for CPIAUCSL-FEDFUNDS interaction term is below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0%), a further increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE rising > 0.2pp in 1 month) signals deteriorating labor market conditions and reduced consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 1 month within high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0%) (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC for UNRATE predicting 20-day returns in this regime is below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.
